figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Gene organization of the vibriomycin gene cluster. The proposed biosynthetic pathway is shown. Domain key: A: adenylation; C:
condensation; Cy: cyclization; PCP: peptidyl carrier protein; KS: ketosynthase; AT: acyltransferase; KR: ketoreductase; DH: dehydratase, ACP:
acyl carrier protein; ER: enoylreductase; cMT: methyltransferase; TE: thioesterase; aaRS: aminoacyl tRNA synthetase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Structures of vibriomycin A (1), B′ (2), B (3), and C (4). Bold bonds indicate COSY correlations and arrows indicate only key HMBC
correlations. For additional correlations see Supporting Information.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Extracted ion chromatogram showing that while KS3 and
the cytochrome P450 (VbrI) are essential for production of
vibriomycin, the methyl transferase, (VbrL) is not.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. (A) Vibriomycin A/B/B′ (1−3) completely inhibits the V. ruber housekeeping threonyl-tRNA synthetase (HKThrRS) at 25 μM whereas
vibriomycin C (4) has no effect at 100 μM. (B) While HKThrRS is susceptible to vibriomycin A/B/B′ (1−3), its self-resistant homologue
(SRThrRS) is resistant to inhibition.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. (A) Michaelis Menten curves for drug-susceptible housekeeping ThrRS (HKThrRS) with various vibriomycin A/B/B′ (1−3)
concentrations and varying threonine concentrations showing noncompetitive inhibition with threonine. (B) IC50 curve of vibriomycin A/B/B′
(1−3) at 5 μM Threonine. (C) Michaelis Menten curves for HKThrRS with various vibriomycin A/B/B′ (1−3) concentrations and varying ATP
concentrations showing noncompetitive inhibition with ATP. (D) IC50 curve of vibriomycin A/B/B′ (1−3) at 600 μM ATP.
